text: The ultrasound shows a thickened endometrial stripe and a left adnexal mass, which raises concern for endometrial pathology or ovarian cancer. I need to check your tumor markers to assess the likelihood of malignancy. REQUEST TEST: CA-125

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the thickened endometrial stripe and postmenopausal bleeding, I need to rule out endometrial cancer. Let's perform an endometrial biopsy to obtain tissue for pathology. REQUEST TEST: Endometrial_Biopsy

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy confirms well-differentiated endometrial adenocarcinoma, which explains the bleeding. Since the adnexal mass persists despite normal CA-125, I need to rule out synchronous ovarian involvement. REQUEST TEST: CT_Abdomen_Pelvis

speaker: Doctor
text: The CT scan is normal, which is reassuring against widespread metastatic disease or a large ovarian primary. speaker: Doctor
text: The imaging confirms a left adnexal mass alongside your endometrial cancer, raising concern for a synchronous ovarian tumor or direct extension. Given the well-differentiated nature of the adenocarcinoma and normal CT findings, this is likely early-stage endometrial cancer with a benign or low-grade adnexal process. DIAGNOSIS READY: Endometrial adenocarcinoma with synchronous adnexal mass
